arxiv-1603-09679.title: Towards co-designed optimizations in parallel frameworks: A MapReduce case study
arxiv-1603-09679.creator: Colin Barrett Christos Kotselidis Mikel Luján
arxiv-1603-09679.description: Abstract The explosion of Big Data was followed by the proliferation of numerous complex parallel software stacks whose aim is to tackle the challenges of data deluge. A drawback of a such multi-layered hierarchical deployment is the inability to maintain and delegate vital semantic information between layers in the stack.

arxiv-1612-00241.title: A biology journal that can teach physicists a lesson in peer review An edited version of this commentary has been published as: R.E. Goldstein, “A biology journal provides a lesson in peer review”, Physics Today 69 (12), 10 (2016).
arxiv-1612-00241.creator: Raymond E. Goldstein
arxiv-1612-00241.description: Abstract After weeks of waiting, the email finally arrives from Physical Review Z with the reports on your paper “A theory of the nonuniform browning of toast”. Hope turns to despair as you read the editor’s cover letter saying that because the reviews contain a sufficiently strong criticism of your paper it cannot be accepted.

arxiv-2005-08299.title: Operator inequalities and characterizations
arxiv-2005-08299.creator: A. Seddik
arxiv-2005-08299.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by A. Seddik. Let 𝔅 ⁡ ( H ) \mathfrak{B}(H) be the C*-algebra of all bounded linear operators acting on a complex separable Hilbert space H H . In this survey, we shall present characterizations of some distinguished classes of 𝔅 ⁡ ( H ) \mathfrak{B}(H) (namely, normal operators, selfadjoint operators, and unitary operators) in terms of operator inequalities related to the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality.

arxiv-2101-06296.title: Sensitivity Prewarping for Local Surrogate Modeling
arxiv-2101-06296.creator: Nathan Wycoff 1 , Mickaël Binois 2 and Robert B. Gramacy 3
arxiv-2101-06296.description: Abstract In the continual effort to improve product quality and decrease operations costs, computational modeling is increasingly being deployed to determine feasibility of product designs or configurations. Surrogate modeling of these computer experiments via local models, which induce sparsity by only considering short range interactions, can tackle huge analyses of complicated input-output relationships.

arxiv-2211-11278.title: Optimal Extended Neighbourhood Rule k k Nearest Neighbours Ensemble
arxiv-2211-11278.creator: Amjad Ali, Zardad Khan, Dost Muhammad Khan Ali, Saeed Aldahmani
arxiv-2211-11278.description: Abstract The traditional k k nearest neighbor ( k k NN) approach uses a distance formula within a spherical region to determine the k k closest training observations to a test sample point. However, this approach may not work well when test point is located outside this region.

arxiv-2212-05935.title: Hierarchical multimodal transformers for Multi-Page DocVQA
arxiv-2212-05935.creator: Rubèn Tito, Dimosthenis Karatzas, Ernest Valveny
arxiv-2212-05935.description: Abstract Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) refers to the task of answering questions from document images. Existing work on DocVQA only considers single-page documents. However, in real scenarios documents are mostly composed of multiple pages that should be processed altogether. In this work we extend DocVQA to the multi-page scenario.

arxiv-2301-09440.title: Splitting Plane Graphs to Outerplanarity Thanks: Anaïs Villedieu is supported by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) under grant P31119. Affiliation: Algorithms and Complexity Group, TU Wien, Vienna, Austria E-mail {mgronemann—noellenburg—avilledieu}@ac.tuwien.ac.at
arxiv-2301-09440.creator: Martin Gronemann, Martin Nöllenburg, Anaïs Villedieu
arxiv-2301-09440.description: Abstract Vertex splitting replaces a vertex by two copies and partitions its incident edges amongst the copies. This problem has been studied as a graph editing operation to achieve desired properties with as few splits as possible, most often planarity, for which the problem is 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard.

arxiv-2503-00568.title: Logica-TGD: Transforming Graph Databases Logically
arxiv-2503-00568.creator: Evgeny Skvortsov, Yilin Xia, Bertram Ludäscher, Shawn Bowers
arxiv-2503-00568.description: Abstract Graph transformations are a powerful computational model for manipulating complex networks, but handling temporal aspects and scalability remain significant challenges. We present a novel approach to implementing these transformations using Logica, an open-source logic programming language and system that operates on parallel databases like DuckDB and BigQuery.

arxiv-2508-00985.title: Metal-Poor Star-Forming Clumps in Cosmic Noon Galaxies: Evidence for Gas Inflow and Chemical Dilution Using JWST NIRISS

Martis, Adam Muzzin, Gaël Noirot, Gregor Rihtaršič, Ghassan T. E. Sarrouh, Chris J. Willott, Jeremy Favaro, Vladan Markov, Rosa M. Mérida, Kather
arxiv-2508-00985.description: Abstract The formation and evolution of galaxies are intricately linked to the baryon cycle, which fuels star formation while shaping chemical abundances within galaxies. Investigating the relationship between star formation and metallicity for large samples of galaxies requires expensive IFU surveys or sophisticated tools to analyze grism data.

arxiv-2510-13564.description: Abstract . However, most of previous studies are mainly focused on the function of TGF-β in immune cells to the development of allergic asthma

pmc-10693890.title: Traditional, complementary and integrative healthcare: global stakeholder perspective on WHO’s current and future strategy
pmc-10693890.creator: Tido von Schoen-Angerer, Raj Kumar Manchanda, Iva Lloyd, Jon Wardle, Janka Szöke, Iracema Benevides, Natalia Sofia Aldana Martinez, Festus Tolo, Ton Nicolai, Cristal Skaling-Klopstock, Tabatha Parker, Dwi Linna Suswardany, Robbert van Haselen, Jianping Liu
pmc-10693890.description: As the ‘WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy: 2014–2023’ is entering its final phase, reflection is warranted on progress and the focus for a new strategy. We used WHO documentation to analyse progress across the objectives of the current strategy, adding the role of traditional, complementary and integrative healthcare (TCIH) to address specific diseases as a dimension absent in the current strategy.

pmc-11418135.title: Transcatheter arterial embolization in postpartum HELLP syndrome: A case report
pmc-11418135.creator: Xusheng Zhou, Qi Shi, Zhijiang Xie, Lei Wang, Liuqin Gao, Jiaying Dai
pmc-11418135.description: IntroductionHemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, and low platelet count (HELLP) syndrome is a pregnancy-related clinical condition characterized by hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and thrombocytopenia, posing significant risks to maternal and fetal safety. Hepatic hematoma with spontaneous rupture and bleeding is a rare but severe complication of HELLP syndrome, with limited reports of hepatic artery intervention and embolization therapy.

pmc-11716796.title: Susceptibility based magnetic resonance imaging for development of neuroimaging biomarkers
pmc-11716796.creator: Lauren F O'Donnell, Suleiman Khan, Hannah Goldman, Sean Murray, Jakub Szabo, Muhammad T Soliman, Michael Llanos, Olivia Cho, Charles Kingsley, Jody Swain, Stanton B Gray, William D Hopkins, Thomas Wisniewski, Jelle Veraart, Henrieta Scholtzova, Youssef Zaim‐Wadghiri
pmc-11716796.description: BackgroundAmyloid related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), a group of neuropathological features seen in anti‐amyloid immunotherapy patients, arises partly from CAA (Aβ buildup in blood vessels). Squirrel monkeys (SQMs), developing prominent age‐related CAA exceeding brain Aβ, offer a unique NHP model for ARIA study.

pmc-12432778.title: Inhibition of SLC25A10 promotes cellular senescence and impedes hepatocellular carcinoma progression
pmc-12432778.creator: Yi-Hong Ding, Tian-Yi Huang, Shi-Meng Xu, Min Li, Xiang Shi, Wen-Yan Sun, Cui-Hua Lu, Zhao-Xiu Liu, Wei Huang
pmc-12432778.description: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality with limited therapeutic options. Solute carrier family 25 member 10 (SLC25A10), a mitochondrial transporter linked to metabolic regulation and tumor progression, has unclear roles in HCC pathogenesis. This study aimed to elucidate the functional and mechanistic contributions of SLC25A10 to HCC development.

pmc-12713194.title: Next-generation antiviral peptides: AI-driven design, translational delivery platforms, and future therapeutic directions

pmc-13538073.title: Evaluating the geographic distribution of rural PFAS contamination and potential dietary sources of exposure
pmc-13538073.creator: Haeseung Yi, Crystal So, Tammy A. Flores, Haley L. Motola, Jill Hubert-Simon, Stella Yi, Vittorio Albergamo, Lorna E. Thorpe, Leonardo Trasande, David C. Lee
pmc-13538073.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aside from specific occupational exposures, ingestion is believed to be the primary route of exposure to PFAS, a class of forever chemicals known for their ability to repel oil and water, reduce friction, and resist high temperatures. The goal was to explore the geographic distribution of PFAS water contamination versus human exposure and identify dietary factors that may explain high PFAS levels among rural residents.

pmc-13556028.title: An animal-derived protein hydrolysate alleviates osmotic stress-induced oxidative damage in tomato by activating ascorbate and glutathione cycle
pmc-13556028.creator: Yinhua Ji, Yifan Fu, Xinyu Yuan, Yang Jiao, Weixuan Wang, Luyao Ma, Haofeng Lv, Bin Liang, Weiwei Zhou
pmc-13556028.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundProtein hydrolysates, as a major group of biostimulants, have gained increasing attention because of their remarkable efficacy in enhancing plant stress resistance. However, the mechanism underlying protein hydrolysate-mediated tolerance to osmotic stress remains poorly understood.
